title: the-librarian-publishes-its-trees-client
intention: The graph-tree store in cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py becomes a client tool the librarian publishes, cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py, whose charter declares published_by_device and public_interface ['cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees']; the LibrarianDevice class moves out of it to cairn/devices/librarian/device.py, and RESOLUTION_FLOOR moves from librarian/loop.py into the tool, so every tenant (cairn/tools/tree, the orient and inspector nexi, codemother's chart machines, skills/moreabout) reaches the trees through the published tool and never into the librarian's insides.
why: RULE 1 child: 16 encapsulation rows reach into the librarian for its graph-tree store and its resolution floor; a client tool the librarian publishes is the declared interface
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes) via parent 8e3474a6ae43; Law 6 (the librarian owns the shared node and embedding tables; each tenant owns its leaf table through db_domain's owner gate — unchanged by the move).
how: Measured 2026-10-02 (encapsulation_breaches('.') in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py): 128 rows; 13 land on cairn.devices.librarian.trees (cairn/tools/tree/tree.py:58, its proof, cairn/tools/orient's and build_inspector's nexus proofs, the seven codemother chart-machine proofs, codemother's test_deposit, skills/moreabout's proof) and 3 on cairn.devices.librarian.loop, every one importing RESOLUTION_FLOOR (tree.py:59, its proof, moreabout's proof). trees.py imports only cairn.tools.base.device (for LibrarianDevice at line 1244) and the db_domain client tool; its functions take an owner and a table, so each tenant's leaf table stays the tenant's, and the shared node and embedding tables stay the librarian's (Law 6). The precedent is db_domain's client (ticket 4cbf6e28126e): a device publishes a nested client tool when graph-tree volume is too heavy for a bus round trip per row. So: git mv trees.py to cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py; cut the device section (from '# ── the device ──' to end) into cairn/devices/librarian/device.py; move RESOLUTION_FLOOR = 0.65 and its comment into the tool, loop.py importing it back; rewrite every importer (17 'from cairn.devices.librarian import trees', 22 'from cairn.devices.librarian.trees import', 1 'import cairn.devices.librarian.trees as trees', LibrarianDevice importers to cairn.devices.librarian.device); write the tool charter through the door. The other tools-reach-devices-over-the-bus rows (operator_inbox -> trouble, codemother.dashboard, harbor_master; system_word -> ground_loop.cli, harbor_master, sudo_relay; tools/base -> bus) are not this ticket's.
falsifier: RED if: (1) the live encapsulation_breaches('.') carries any row whose module is cairn.devices.librarian.trees or cairn.devices.librarian.loop; (2) any .py file names the module cairn.devices.librarian.trees (dotted, or 'from cairn.devices.librarian import trees'), or cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py exists, or the tool module defines a class LibrarianDevice; (3) cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/intention+why.json does not carry published_by_device true and public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees'], or the tool imports anything from cairn.devices other than cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client, or it does not expose deposit, nearest, neighbors, scratch_leaf, NODES and RESOLUTION_FLOOR, or cairn.devices.librarian.loop.RESOLUTION_FLOOR is not the tool's value, or cairn.devices.librarian.device.LibrarianDevice is missing. WRONG INTENT if a tenant needs the librarian to ACT (not just store) where a client tool cannot carry it. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py.
watchme: none, because the encapsulation_holds sieve in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py reds any new reach into the librarian at the next inspect, and the store's behaviour is exercised by every proof that already deposits or walks
children: none, because the move is one file split in two plus a dotted-path rewrite; the other tools-reach-devices-over-the-bus clusters are siblings cast as reached
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? git mv cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py; empty __init__.py in tools/ and tools/trees/; the device section moves to cairn/devices/librarian/device.py. (2) What? sed the three import forms to the tool's path; LibrarianDevice importers to cairn.devices.librarian.device. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py, PROVES keys 1, 2, 3, red first.
